findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O errors (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing input file aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or typed domain error) and propagate with ? or explicit map_err; never unwrap external I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input and on missing second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (no second column or non-numeric value) aborts the parser instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') or checked indexing with get(), then parse with .map_err() returning a typed Parse error; propagate failure per record or as a batch Result

findings.problem: Lossy width cast `as u16` from u32 to u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A u32 value of 70000 becomes 4464 silently, corrupting telemetry data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and return a typed Overflow/ConversionError on out-of-range values

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked array indexing; a line with no comma (0 parts after split) panics at runtime
findings.failure_mode: Malformed line with no comma causes index-out-of-bounds panic instead of a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the Some((name, rest)) / None pattern; reject lines without exactly one comma with a typed error

findings.problem: println!() (I/O side-effect) is embedded in the data-parsing pipeline alongside allocation and indexing
findings.failure_mode: Side-effects in core data processing make the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and mixes imperative shell concerns into data loading
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing path; if telemetry logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell layer as an explicit post-processing action or dedicated logger call

findings.problem: Collects every CSV field into Vec<String> via map+collect before accessing only the first two fields
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation of all split parts per line; a line with many trailing commas allocates a Vec of all parts when only two are needed
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get exactly two parts without collecting all fields; avoid Vec<String> allocation entirely for simple two-field records

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity hint for the output Vec; unknown file size means potential reallocations
findings.failure_mode: Large telemetry files cause repeated Vec reallocations, degrading performance; allocation failure is silently handled by OOM panic
findings.fix: If file length is available, use Vec::with_capacity after checked arithmetic on line count; otherwise accept reallocation but document the tradeoff

findings.problem: The function mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, and side-effects (println!) into a single API with no error type
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish I/O failure from parse failure from data validation failure; no typed error taxonomy exists
findings.fix: Split into: (1) pure `parse_record(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>` in the core, (2) `load_telemetry(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, TelemetryError>` in the shell that handles I/O, maps errors, and performs logging

findings.problem: Record uses owned String for name; no value-object newtype guards the name domain rules
findings.failure_mode: Any string can be assigned to name, including empty strings, null bytes, or domain-invalid values; no compile-time guarantee on name validity
findings.fix: Introduce a `RecordName` newtype with a fallible constructor that enforces domain invariants (non-empty, no nulls, max length); use `RecordName` in Record

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation tracking infrastructure present in the crate
findings.failure_mode: No empirical evidence to verify allocation behavior, parsing throughput, or correctness of performance decisions
findings.fix: Add a criterion or built-in benchmark for parse_record with synthetic CSV inputs of varying size; measure allocations with --features=tracing or `dhat`

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for parsing throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf) to validate allocation hotspots
no allocation tracking (dhat, jemalloc profiling) for Vec growth patterns
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
no second-ring review (black-hat review, formal verification) evidence
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. Multiple BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy cast, unchecked indexing, and I/O side-effects in the data pipeline. The function as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or out-of-range value. Requires full rewrite per Holzman Rust: typed errors, checked conversions, split_once over collect, pure core parsing, and shell-layer I/O with no println in the parse path.
